references.text: The same chapter describes the place the Lord will choose to put His name there and emphasizes the centralization of worship.
Repeats the theme of bringing offerings to the place the Lord chooses, directly paralleling verse 11.
Mentions tithes and vows, as well as the place where the Lord causes His name to dwell, corresponding with the themes in Deuteronomy 12:11.
Describes offering sacrifices at the place the Lord chooses to put His name there, using identical wording to 12:11.
Concerns bringing the first fruits to the place the Lord chooses to put His name there, parallel to the offering command in 12:11.
Solomon's prayer at the temple dedication refers to the place where the Lord's name will dwell, fulfilling the promise from Deuteronomy.
God says He chose Shiloh as the place where His name would dwell, referencing the concept from Deuteronomy 12:11.
The command to bring offerings to the tent of meeting corresponds with the centralization of worship described in Deuteronomy 12:11.
Mentions giving the best of the gifts as a holy offering to the Lord, parallel to 'the best of their vows' in Deuteronomy 12:11.
Describes the first covenant's worship arrangements and the earthly sanctuary, which are built upon the sacrificial laws from Deuteronomy.
